target_customer: Data center operators who dispatch technicians for inspection, cable checks and hardware swaps
problem: Data centers need physical remote-hands work and monitoring; Boost builds autonomous mobile manipulation robots that inspect and physically work on infrastructure.
business_model: Robot hardware and service via pilots with data centers; pricing not found
product_category: Mobile manipulation robots for data centers

founders.name: Hardik Singh
education: MS Robotic Systems Development, Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; employer name not given.

founders.name: Hans Kumar
prior_employers: Boston Dynamics (Staff Software Engineer, computer vision for Spot inspection)

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous mobile manipulation in dense rack environments needs perception, dexterous manipulation and safety around critical hardware; the product was still a prototype seeking pilots per search results.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus manipulation software is hard to replicate quickly, but well-funded robotics firms could enter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Boston Dynamics Spot was used for data center inspection and security, but not for manipulation; no incumbent outcome for Boost recorded.

market_need_then: Rapid AI data center buildout increased demand for inspection and maintenance labor; Boston Dynamics reported rising data center interest in 2026 coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses boostrobotics.ai; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short and confident; tagline 'Digital Infra. Physical Agents.'

branding.community_and_virality: None found. Search results are confused with Booster Robotics, an unrelated Beijing humanoid maker.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage and a name easily confused with Booster Robotics.

outcome_analysis: Boost Robotics is a two person Spring 2025 YC company founded by CMU robotics graduates, one of whom worked on Spot at Boston Dynamics, building robots for data center remote hands work. No verified funding, customers or exit were found, and the product was described as a prototype seeking pilots, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked and StartupIntros list a 500K dollar round (pre-seed or seed) in June 2025, aggregator only. Competitors found by search (Exclaim Robotics, Spot users, Ghost Robotics) lack dates near the batch, so the list is empty; later entrants include Watney, Aformic and Exclaim. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news found. Founder bios come from the YC page.
